primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Familial hypercholesterolemia due to LDLR loss of function
mechanism: LDLR loss of function reduces hepatic clearance of circulating LDL particles. LDL receptors normally bind apoB-100-containing LDL and mediate receptor-dependent uptake, so impaired receptor function causes marked lifelong elevation of LDL cholesterol and premature atherosclerosis.
vignette: A young adult has markedly elevated LDL cholesterol, tendon xanthomas, and a strong family history of premature coronary artery disease. Genetic testing identifies a pathogenic loss-of-function variant in LDLR.
lead: Which of the following cellular processes is most directly reduced by this mutation?
correct: Receptor-mediated uptake of circulating LDL particles by hepatocytes
distractors: ABCA1-mediated cholesterol efflux from peripheral cells to apolipoprotein A-I
LCAT-mediated esterification of cholesterol within HDL particles
Lipoprotein-lipase-mediated hydrolysis of triglycerides in chylomicrons
Microsomal triglyceride-transfer-protein-mediated assembly of apoB-containing lipoproteins
distractor_notes: ABCA1-mediated cholesterol efflux is impaired in Tangier disease and is part of reverse cholesterol transport, not the primary LDLR defect.
LCAT esterifies free cholesterol on HDL; its deficiency produces a distinct HDL-related disorder.
Lipoprotein lipase hydrolyzes triglycerides in chylomicrons and VLDL and does not mediate hepatic LDL clearance.
MTTP assembles apoB-containing lipoproteins; MTTP deficiency causes abetalipoproteinemia rather than elevated LDL.
key_expl: The LDL receptor is a major determinant of plasma LDL clearance. Hepatocyte LDL receptors bind apoB-100-containing LDL and internalize the particle through receptor-mediated uptake. Loss-of-function LDLR variants therefore reduce LDL clearance, producing lifelong LDL elevation, xanthomas, and premature atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.
objective: Relate LDLR loss of function in familial hypercholesterolemia to reduced receptor-mediated hepatic clearance of circulating LDL.
